rationale: Archive the Valor Compute Infrastructure record and retire its purported Apollo ownership because Valor Compute Infrastructure L.P. is a pooled private-equity fund managed by Valor, not an Apollo-owned operating company or infrastructure platform. Apollo led an asset-backed capital solution. An Apollo private-credit vehicle also held small non-controlling equity interests in downstream numbered financing SPVs, so the original debt-only rationale is incomplete; however, those financing exposures do not establish Apollo ownership or control of VCI L.P. The approved archive overlay removes the evaluated seed entry, while the database preserves an archived audit record and its corrected relations rather than deleting history.

beforeImage.name: Valor Compute Infrastructure (VCI)
beforeImage.description: Valor Compute Infrastructure is an investment vehicle created to acquire and lease data center compute infrastructure used in AI workloads. The platform serves large-scale digital infrastructure demand through an asset-heavy leasing model rather than through conventional retail colocation or managed hosting services. Apollo stated in January 2026 that VCI was part of a $5.4 billion transaction to acquire and lease NVIDIA GB200 GPU infrastructure to an xAI subsidiary under a triple-net structure. The disclosed scale makes the platform a specialized owner-lessor of high-value compute equipment tied to next-generation data center demand. Apollo announced that it led a $3.5 billion capital solution for VCI in January 2026, while public sources do not disclose the current ownership percentages within the vehicle.

milestones.event: The transaction was structured as a triple-net lease arrangement tied to AI compute infrastructure.
Apollo announced a $3.5 billion capital solution for Valor Compute Infrastructure.

afterImage.name: Valor Compute Infrastructure (VCI)
afterImage.description: Archived census record for Valor Compute Infrastructure L.P., a Delaware pooled private-equity fund formed in 2025 and managed by Valor Management LLC, with Valor CI Associates L.P. as general partner. The fund acquires compute infrastructure for leasing to an xAI subsidiary. Apollo led an asset-backed capital solution, and an Apollo private-credit vehicle also held small non-controlling equity interests in downstream numbered financing SPVs; no public evidence establishes Apollo ownership or control of VCI L.P. or an Apollo infrastructure-equity portfolio company. The record is therefore excluded from the PortCo census.
